content:
RESOLVED
that
 
1.       the
freehold sale of Rentwood, School Lane, Fetcham, KT22 9JX and 37
School Lane, Fetcham, KT22 9JX, to the party, at the price and
subject to the terms set out in exempt Appendix A of the report, be
approved;
 
2.       in
accordance with approval from the Halsey Garton Residential (HGR)
Ltd. Board, the surrender of the headlease interest affecting 37
School Lane, held by HGR, be approved, and it be noted that an
associated premium will be payable from the gross capital receipt
and that there is debt aligned to this asset, with parties bearing
their own costs and appointments of their own professional team, as
set out within exempt Appendix A of the report;
 
3.      
authority be delegated to Surrey County Council’s Deputy
Chief Executive and Executive Director of Resources (s151 Officer),
in consultation with Surrey County Council’s Director of Land
& Property and Surrey County Council’s Cabinet Member for
Property, Waste and Infrastructure, to finalise the transaction and
enter into all associated legal agreements necessary to implement
the transaction on the terms set out in Exempt Appendix A of the
report; and
 
4.       it
be noted that Surrey County Council’s Cabinet previously
endorsed rationalisation of the surplus estate and on 28 July 2026
declared the assets formally surplus to operational requirements
under Surrey County Council’s Constitution with 37 School
Lane having previously been declared surplus to operational
requirements by Surrey County Council’s Strategic Investment
Board (SIB) on 16 June 2025.

RESOLVED
that
 
1.      
Mole Valley District Council be granted consent to exercise its option to extend its Leisure Centres contract with
Greenwich Leisure Limited by five years to 2043;
and
 
2.       in
accordance with 1. above, authority be delegated to Mole Valley
District Council’s Executive Head of Service (Commercial), in
consultation with the Mole Valley District Council Cabinet Member
for Leisure, to agree the terms of, and enter into, all necessary
and ancillary agreements.

RESOLVED
that
 
1.       it
be noted that the statutory responsibilities for electoral
registration and election delivery rest with the Electoral
Registration Officer and Returning Officer respectively;
 
2.       it
be noted that East Surrey Council must provide the funding and
resources required to enable the Electoral Registration Officer and
Returning Officer to discharge their functions; and
 
3.      
subject to the Shadow Executive’s approval of recommendations
4 to 8 below, the migration costs will be drawn from the LGR
Implementation Fund;
 
4.       the
principle of procuring and implementing a single Electoral
Management System for East Surrey Council to support the safe and
lawful delivery of electoral registration and elections from
vesting day, be approved;
 
5.       the
preferred procurement route for the East Surrey Electoral
Management System be via a direct award through a framework
agreement, with an initial contract term of three years and a
one-year optional extension;
 
6.       the
principle of procuring and implementing a single electoral print
supplier for East Surrey Council, to align with the single
Electoral Management System and support the production of statutory
electoral documents, be approved;
 
7.       the
preferred procurement route for the East Surrey electoral print
contract be an open tender, with an initial contract term of two
years and a one-year optional extension;
 
8.       the
interim S151 officer for East Surrey ensure that the financial
implications of the new contracts are reflected in the 2027/28
budget as part of the budget setting process; and
 
9.      
Section 24 consent be granted for any existing sovereign
authorities to enter into a new 12 month contract with their
existing providers of electoral management software where the terms
of their existing contract cannot be extended to 31 March 2028
whilst a procurement for the new system is undertaken.

RESOLVED
that
 
1.       it
be noted that Surrey County Council has received the Experts at
Hand grant provided by the Department of Education to implement
elements of the SEND Reform programme for the 2026/27 financial
year, and that both East Surrey and West Surrey Councils will
receive their equivalent value of this grant in both 2027/28 and
2028/29;
 
2.      
consent be granted to Surrey County Council, under Section 24 of
the Local Government and Public Involvement in Health Act 2007, to
commission a specialist outreach offer and Alternative Provision
Specialist Taskforce, as part of the Experts at Hand model;
and
 
3.       in
accordance with 2. above, Surrey County Council be requested to
publish it’s SEND Reform Plan at the earliest opportunity,
together with the Government’s response when received, and
further clarification be provided on the issues raised above,
including the potential impact on specialist school
resources.

RESOLVED
that consent be granted, under Section 24 of the
Local Government and Public Involvement in Health Act 2007, to Mole
Valley District Council to:
 
1.       dispose of 23 High
Street, Leatherhead;
 
2.      
negotiate any variances up to 20% on the disposal contract value;
and
 
3.      
finalise all contractual details and enter into all contracts in
relation to the disposal, as required under its
constitution.

RESOLVED
that
 
1.      
subject to a similar resolution being made by the West Surrey
Shadow Authority, the recommended configuration of services to
transition to East Surrey Council and West Surrey Council, as set
out in Appendix 1 of the report, by Programme Theme, be supported,
and include the basis for further transition work, including which
services should be:
 
·        
disaggregated between East Surrey Council and West
Surrey Council;
·        
aggregated into East Surrey Council and West Surrey
Council, based on geography;
·        
hosted by either East Surrey Council or West Surrey
Council, on behalf of both, on a temporary basis, with defined
review points;
·        
retained ‘whole’ in the longer term,
including those transferring to the Combined Fire and Rescue
Authority and Pensions Authority;
·        
hosted specifically by East Surrey Council on behalf
of both East Surrey Council and West Surrey Council, or hosted
specifically by West Surrey Council on behalf of both East Surrey
Council and West Surrey Council, where there is an operational
rationale for such an arrangement;
 
         
and that a further report will be brought back to the Shadow
Executive in September 2026 recommending Appendix 1 for agreement,
with further detail on the recommended proportionate split of
disaggregating services to follow;
 
2.       the
principles being used to recommend the proportionate split of
activity for disaggregated services between East Surrey Council and
West Surrey Council, as set out in the report, be noted, and that
recommendations on the basis of application of these will be
brought to the Shadow Executive for agreement in Autumn
2026;
 
3.       the
proposed approach to determining which of East Surrey Council or
West Surrey Council will be the host authority for services where
no clear location-based rationale exists, as set out in this
report, be agreed;
 
4.      
authority be delegated to the Head of Paid Service, in consultation
with the Leader of East Surrey Shadow Authority, relevant Portfolio
Holders and the Senior Responsible Officer, to revisit and amend
any recommended service configurations should this become necessary
in light of central government direction and/or delivery
requirements;
 
5.       it
be noted that material budget pressures and potential savings
arising from the recommended service configurations will be
identified and included for consideration within the wider
strategic and financial planning process; and
 
6.       it
be noted that West Surrey Shadow Executive was also considering
this report at their equivalent meeting on 21 July 2026, and that
decisions taken by each authority will necessitate ongoing joint
working across the Shadow Executives throughout the shadow
transition period to support a successful
implementation.
topline: The UK council has decided to support the transition of services to East Surrey Council and West Surrey Council, with further details to be provided in a future report.

content:
RESOLVED
that
 
1.       the
harmonisation of local Council Tax Support Schemes across East
Surrey from 1 April 2027 be agreed, in principle;
 
2.       the
undertaking of comprehensive modelling of options to inform the
final proposals, utilising external expertise be agreed, and for
modelling purposes, the central case, as set in paragraph 12 of the
report, be used as the benchmark for scheme modelling to compare
the cost of different schemes;
 
3.      
having considered the recommendation from the Overview &
Scrutiny Committee following its review of the item at its meeting
on 8 July 2026, officers be asked to provide a full assessment of
the impact of the preferred option on vulnerable households as part
of the development of the harmonised Council Tax Support scheme;
and
 
4.      
authority be delegated to the Section 151 Officer to complete all
procurement activities and enter relevant contracts in relation to
the work set out in 2. above.
topline: The council has decided to harmonise local Council Tax Support Schemes across East Surrey, potentially impacting vulnerable households.

content:
RESOLVED
that
 

1.       in principle,
discretionary Council Tax and Business Rates policies be harmonised
across East Surrey from vesting day;
 

2.       the adoption of a
single harmonised Section 13A(1)(c) discretionary policy for East
Surrey, applying a consistent framework for hardship, exceptional
circumstances, application requirements, evidence, decision-making,
review and appeals be endorsed;
 

3.       the adoption of a
single harmonised Section 47 discretionary Business Rates Relief
policy for East Surrey, covering charitable and not-for-profit
relief, community and economic benefit, hardship relief, local
discounts, Government-funded schemes administered through Section
47 powers and subsidy control requirements, be endorsed;
 

4.       it be noted that the
workstream lead will develop and finalise the policy wording,
implementation plan, operational guidance and undertake any
necessary consultation, in consultation with the Section 151
Officer and Monitoring Officer, ahead of formal future approval of
the revised policies through the appropriate decision-making route;
and
 
5.       the
harmonised policies be reviewed within twelve months of 1 April
2027, and thereafter at least every three years or sooner where
legislative, financial or operational changes require
review.
topline: The council has decided to harmonise discretionary Council Tax and Business Rates policies across East Surrey

content:
RESOLVED
that consent be given to Elmbridge Borough Council
and Mole Valley District Council to award the bidder that submitted
the most advantageous tender (Preferred Bidder) the joint contract
to deliver waste collection and street cleansing services in
Elmbridge and Mole Valley (Joint Contract) commencing from 6 June
2027 up to and including 5 June 2034, with the option, but not the
obligation, for the participating authorities and the service
provider to agree to extend the Joint Contract by one or more
successive consecutive periods until 2048 and in doing so, the
following be agreed:
 
a.      
Elmbridge Borough Council and Mole Valley District Council enter
the Joint Contract with each of the partner authorities, (Woking
Borough Council and Surrey Heath Borough Council) and the Preferred
Bidder (such contract inter alia providing that the partner
authorities will have joint and several liability to the service
provider and against which they indemnify each other against their
breach);
 
b.      
Elmbridge Borough Council and Mole Valley District Council enter
into the Inter-Authority Agreement (IAA) with each of the other
partner authorities, Woking Borough Council and Surrey Heath
Borough Council, which will regulate the relationship between the
partner authorities (as necessitated by entry into the Joint
Contract), continues the role of the shared contract management
office (hosted by Surrey Heath Borough Council as the administering
authority) and the required governance arrangements, including the
terms of reference for the Joint Waste Collection Services
Committee;
 
c.      
pursuant to section 9EA of the Local Government Act 2000,
Regulations 9 and 11 of the Local Authorities (Arrangements for the
Discharge of Functions)(England) 2012 and all other enabling powers
of the functions of the Council under section 45 of the
Environmental Protection Act 1990, Elmbridge Borough Council and
Mole Valley District Council make arrangements for the joint
discharge of such of those functions as are set out in the
Inter-Authority Agreement by the Joint Waste Collection Services
Committee established for that purpose;
 
d.       the
provisions of the Contract Management Office provided in the
Inter-Authority Agreement is entered into as a contract for
services in order to deliver co-operation between public bodies as
envisaged by Schedule 2 of the Procurement Act 2023;
 
e.       the
authorities grant a lease of part of Mill Road depot (Esher) and a
lease of part of Station Road (Dorking) depot at a peppercorn rent
to the Preferred Bidder commencing on 6 June 2027 and co-terminus
with the Council’s participation in the Joint
Contract;
 
f.        the
authorities will incur the capital cost of replacing the vehicles
to deliver the services as set out in Appendix 2, noting that this
was built into the approved capital strategies for each of
Elmbridge Borough Council and Mole Valley District Council, and
will need to be included in the 2027/28 capital programme for East
Surrey;
 
g.       the
2027/28 budget for East Surrey will need to factor in an increase
in the revenue budget for Waste Services as set out in Appendix 2;
and
 
h.      
authority be delegated to the Deputy Chief Executive and Strategic
Director (Place and Community) at Elmbridge Borough Council and the
Executive Head of Service (Commercial) at Mole Valley District
Council to make all decisions and take all actions in respect of
any agreements or other instruments as are reasonably necessary to
give effect to (or are ancillary to) the above resolutions of East
Surrey Shadow Authority, on behalf of Elmbridge Borough Council and
Mole Valley District Council.
topline: The East Surrey Shadow Authority has decided to award a joint contract for waste collection and street cleansing services in Elmbridge and Mole Valley

content:
RESOLVED
that
 
1.       a
harmonised approach to Council Tax Premiums across all constituent
authorities, be adopted;
 
2.       a 100% premium on
second homes be applied from 1 April 2027;
 
3.      
long-term empty property premiums be applied at the maximum levels
permitted by legislation for properties which are empty and
unfurnished:
 
         
a.   100% premium for properties
empty for 1 to 5 years;
         
b.   200% premium for properties
empty for 5 to 10 years;
         
c.   300% premium for properties
empty for more than 10 years.
 
4.       all
mandatory statutory exemptions be maintained and the use of
discretionary reliefs be reviewed to ensure consistency across East
Surrey.
topline: The UK council has decided to adopt a harmonised approach to Council Tax Premiums, apply a 100% premium on second homes, and increase premiums for long-term empty properties.

content:
Resolved that
 
(a)           
the results of the consultation on proposals to
extend Public Spaces Protection Orders (PSPOs), be
noted;
 
(b)      having
been satisfied on reasonable grounds that the statutory conditions
for making such an Order were still necessary to prevent an
occurrence or recurrence of the activities identified in that
Order, or to prevent an increase in the frequency or seriousness of
those activities, the Elmbridge Borough Council (Barbeques, etc. or
Lighting of Fires) Public Spaces Protection Order 2023, be extended
in accordance with Sections 60 and 72 of the Anti-Social Behaviour,
Crime and Policing Act 2014;
 
(c)      having
been satisfied on reasonable grounds that the statutory conditions
for making such an Order were still necessary to prevent an
occurrence or recurrence of the activities identified in that
Order, or to prevent an increase in the frequency or seriousness of
those activities, the Elmbridge Borough Council (Overnight Fishing)
Public Spaces Protection Order 2023, be extended in accordance with
Sections 60 and 72 of the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing
Act 2014;
 
(d)      in
accordance with (b) and (c) above, the Public Spaces Protection
Orders be extended for a maximum of 3 years, expiring in July 2029;
and
 
(e)      officers
be authorised to carry out the necessary steps to publicise the
extension of the Public Spaces Protection Order.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to extend Public Spaces Protection Orders related to barbeques, lighting of fires, and overnight fishing in Elmbridge Borough Council.

and

content:
Resolved that the bidder that
submitted the most advantageous tender (Preferred Bidder) be
awarded the Joint Contract to deliver waste collection and street
cleansing services in Elmbridge (Joint Contract) commencing from 6
June 2027 up to and including 5 June 2034, with the option, but not
the obligation, for the participating authorities and the service
provider to agree to extend the Joint Contract by one or more
successive consecutive periods until 2048 and in doing so, the
following be agreed:
 
(a)      the
Council enter into the Joint Contract with each of the partner
authorities and the Preferred Bidder (such contract inter alia
providing that the partner authorities will have joint and several
liability to the contractor and against which they indemnify each
other against their breach);
 
(b)      the
Council enter into the Inter-Authority Agreement with each of the
other partner authorities, Mole Valley, Surrey Heath and Woking
Councils, which will regulate the relationship between the partner
authorities (as necessitated by entry into the Joint Contract),
continues the role of the shared contract management office (hosted
by Surrey Heath Borough Council as the administering authority) and
the required governance arrangements, including the terms of
reference for the Joint Waste Collection Services
Committee;
 
(c)      pursuant
to section 9EA of the Local Government Act 2000, Regulations 9 and
11 of the Local Authorities (Arrangements for the Discharge of
Functions) (England) 2012 and all other enabling powers of the
functions of the Council under Section 45 of the Environmental
Protection Act 1990, the Council make arrangements for the joint
discharge of such of those functions as set out in the
Inter-Authority Agreement by the Joint Waste Collection Services
Committee established for that purpose;
 
(d)      that the
provisions of the Contract Management Office provided in the
Inter-Authority Agreement is entered into as a contract for
services in order to deliver co-operation between public bodies as
envisaged by Schedule 2 of the Procurement Act 2023;
 
(e)      the
Council grants a lease of part of Mill Road depot to the Preferred
Bidder commencing on 6 June 2027 and co-terminus with the
Council’s participation in the Joint Contract;
 
(f)      
that the cost of the vehicles, as set out in Appendix 2 of the
report, be included in the 2027/28 capital programme for East
Surrey Council;
 
(g)     
authority be delegated to the Deputy Chief Executive &
Strategic Director of Place and Community to make all decisions and
take all actions in respect of any agreements or other instruments
as are reasonably necessary to give effect to (or are ancillary to)
the above on behalf of the Council;
 
(h)      pursuant
to the direction made under section 24 of the Local Government and
Public Involvement in Health Act 2007, it be recommended to the
East Surrey Shadow Authority Executive that it approves the
recommendations set out in this report; and
 
(i)      
authority be delegated to the Head of Legal & Governance
(Monitoring Officer), in consultation with the Leader of the
Council, to implement any actions necessary to achieve the
recommendations of this report, including any changes to the
Council’s Constitution.
topline: The Council has decided to award the Joint Contract for waste collection and street cleansing services in Elmbridge to the Preferred Bidder.

(a)      
the report of the Monitoring Officer about irregularities in two

content:
Resolved that
 
(a)       it
be noted that an error occurred in the parking enforcement process
affecting the issue of certain Penalty Charge Notices, while the
underlying requirement to pay and display for parking at the
relevant locations remained valid;
 
(b)       as
a result of the error, the affected Penalty Charge Notices had no
legal effect and the Council was therefore not entitled to the sums
received in payment of those Penalty Charge Notices, and so,
refunds should reasonably be issued where payment has been
made;
 
(c)        the
implementation of a discretionary Penalty Charge Notice Refund
Scheme covering Penalty Charge Notices issued during the defined
period in which the incorrect process was applied, be
approved;
 
(d)      
the Refund Scheme, as attached at Appendix 1 of the report, be
adopted;
 
(e)      
authority be delegated to the Strategic Director for Services, in
consultation with the Portfolio Holder for Enterprise, Parking
& Local Economy, the Chief Finance Officer and the Monitoring
Officer, to revise the scope, eligibility criteria and operating
arrangements for the Refund Scheme after its launch (should
feedback from customers or circumstances require it); determine the
most proportionate method for processing refunds and take any
necessary operational steps to implement the Scheme;
 
(f)        it be noted
that a provision of £80,000 will be made in the 2025/26
accounts for the refunds representing approximately 25% of the
maximum which could be reclaimed, £307,539. A council in the
South East had a similar scheme and based on the refunds that they
issued the provision should be sufficient to cover the likely level
of refunds. The refunds will be monitored and reported in line with
the Council’s financial governance arrangements, and
adjustments may be required to the provision based on the Councils
actual refunds;
 
(g)       it
be noted that learning from the error is incorporated into parking
enforcement processes to prevent recurrence; and
 
(h)       it
be noted that reports back to Cabinet on the effectiveness of the
Refund Scheme will be made on a quarterly basis.
topline: The council has decided to implement a refund scheme for Penalty Charge Notices issued in error.

purpose:
This report sets out the impact of the
Renters' Rights Act 2025 on the Council’s housing enforcement
responsibilities ahead of its commencement on 1 May 2026. It
outlines the key legislative changes, including the
Government’s shift towards a stronger, enforcement-led
regulatory framework for the private rented sector. The report
presents a revised Housing Enforcement Policy for approval to
ensure the Council complies with the new statutory requirements and
operates within a clear and consistent enforcement
framework.
content:
Resolved that
 
(a)      
the Housing Enforcement Policy, as set out in Appendix 1 of the
report, be adopted with effect from 1 May 2026;
 
(b)      
for a six-moth interim period, the existing and revised policies
run concurrently, with cases received before 1 May 2026 handled
under the existing policy and all cases received on or after 1 May
2026 being handled under the revised policy, ensuring clarity,
fairness and consistency in decision-making; and
 
(c)        authority be
delegated to the Head of Housing Services, in consultation with the
Portfolio Holder for Housing, to make any final minor amendments to
the policy that may be necessary prior to publication and to make
any further revisions necessary relating to the second phase of
measures being introduced by the Renters’ Rights Act which
were likely to come into force in late 2026.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to adopt a new Housing Enforcement Policy with a transition period for existing cases.
